category: CAD Import Module, ECAD Import Module and LiveLink products (CAD, Excel, Simulink)
description: COMSOL 6.4 CAD Import Module (3D CAD import options, supported formats, Check, Detect Interferences and the defeaturing tools Delete Short Edges/Sliver Faces/Small Faces/Spikes, Detach and Replace Faces with their find/delete API), ECAD Import Module (IPC-2581, ODB++ and GDS-II import with layer stackup, nets and pads, OASIS export), the CAD LiveLinks (SOLIDWORKS, AutoCAD, Revit, Inventor, Solid Edge, PTC Creo Parametric) with their CAD-side windows and offline synchronization, LiveLink for Excel (worksheet interface, material export, workbook exchange, VBA API) and LiveLink for Simulink (FMU-based cosimulation). API types come from the product programming references and completion data.

tools.name: 3D CAD import options (Import node: knit, repair, simplify, assembly components, CAD selections)
tools.description: Settings of the geometry Import node for 3D CAD files (type cad, CAD kernel): which object types to import (solids, surfaces, curves/points), knitting of surfaces into solids, automatic error fixing, removal of small details, healing of tolerant edges, tolerance minimization, removal of redundant entities, simplification of curve/surface manifolds, unit handling, STEP body names, assembly component selection with preview, and import of named CAD selections and colors. Associativity preserves physics settings when the file is reimported.
tools.usage: Home/Geometry toolbar > Import > Source: 3D CAD file > Browse > Import; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("imp1", "Import"); set("filename", ...); importData()

parameters.name: keepsolid / keepbnd / keepfree
parameters.description: Import solids (on), surfaces (on), curves and points (off).

parameters.name: knit
parameters.description: solid (default) | surface | off - knit imported surfaces.

parameters.name: fixerrors / deletedetails / healedges / minimizetol / removeredundant / simplify
parameters.description: Repair and cleanup options applied on import.

parameters.name: importtol / unit
parameters.description: Absolute repair tolerance (1e-5) and source or current length unit.

parameters.name: importbodynames
parameters.description: auto | on | off - include STEP body names in object names.

parameters.name: assemnodeimport / selcadkeepobj / selcadkeepbnd
parameters.description: Assembly components to import; keep named object/boundary selections from the CAD file.

tools.notes: Periodic faces (full cylinders) are split on import because the mesher needs nonperiodic entities; hide the extra edges with Ignore Edges. The existing 'CAD Import (STEP / IGES / ...)' entry is a shorter overview.

tools.name: Supported 3D CAD file formats (CAD Import Module 6.4)
tools.description: 3D CAD formats readable with the CAD Import Module, Design Module or a CAD LiveLink in COMSOL 6.4: ACIS (.sat, .sab, up to 2025 1.0), AutoCAD (.dwg, .dxf 2.5-2026), CATIA V5 (.CATPart, .CATProduct R8-R2025, needs the File Import for CATIA V5 add-on), IGES (.igs/.iges up to 5.3), Inventor (.ipt 6-2026, .iam 11-2026), NX (.prt up to 2506), Parasolid (.x_t, .x_b up to V38), PTC Creo Parametric (.prt/.asm 1-12), Pro/ENGINEER (16-Wildfire 5), SOLIDWORKS (.sldprt/.sldasm 98-2025) and STEP (AP203E1, AP214, AP242). All of these require a CAD Import Module, Design Module or CAD LiveLink license.
tools.usage: Geometry > Import > Source: 3D CAD file (file type detected from the extension)

parameters.name: Platform notes
parameters.description: Some readers (AutoCAD, CATIA, Inventor, NX, SOLIDWORKS) are available only on Windows/Linux x86-64; ACIS/IGES/STEP/Creo also on macOS.

parameters.name: Assembly preview
parameters.description: Preview and select components for CATIA V5, Inventor, NX, Creo, Pro/E and SOLIDWORKS assemblies.

tools.example: Import a SOLIDWORKS assembly (.sldasm) without SOLIDWORKS installed: Import > Browse > select file > Preview > deselect fasteners in the assembly tree > Import.
tools.notes: Educational-version SOLIDWORKS files are not supported. Export is limited to Parasolid, ACIS, IGES and STEP.

tools.name: Check (CAD objects)
tools.description: Geometry feature that checks CAD-kernel objects for faults such as tolerance problems and invalid entities, reporting each issue as a warning node with Zoom to Selection for the faulty edges or faces. Warnings do not always make the geometry unusable but often explain later Boolean or meshing failures.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Check; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("ch1", "Check")

parameters.name: input (selection)
parameters.description: Objects to check (manual, all objects, all nonconstruction objects).

tools.notes: Follow up with Repair (existing entry) or the defeaturing tools on the reported entities.

tools.name: Detect Interferences (CAD Import Module)
tools.description: Tools-window operation that searches the exterior faces of selected objects for intersections, touches, containments and gaps (within an intersection tolerance of 0.1 mm and a gap tolerance of 1 mm by default), listing interfering faces so assemblies can be cleaned before Form Union. It does not modify the geometry.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Detect Interferences (Tools window) > Find Interferences; API properties input, abstol, gaptol, showintersections, showtouches, showgaps, showcontainments

parameters.name: abstol
parameters.description: Absolute tolerance for intersections (default 0.1 mm).

parameters.name: gaptol
parameters.description: Absolute tolerance for gaps (default 1 mm).

parameters.name: showingraphics / groupbyobject
parameters.description: Which objects to display and grouping of the result list.

tools.example: Import an assembly of 40 parts, run Detect Interferences with gap tolerance 0.05 mm, and fix listed gaps between the heat sink and the chip with Replace Faces or Offset Faces before Form Union.
tools.notes: Interior faces, isolated edges and points are ignored.

tools.name: Delete Short Edges (CAD defeaturing)
tools.description: Finds edges shorter than a maximum length in CAD objects and removes them by merging adjacent vertices and healing the surrounding faces, eliminating tiny mesh constraints that cause very small elements. Found edges can be deleted individually or all at once, each deletion becoming a DeleteShortEdges feature in the sequence.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Delete Short Edges (Tools window: Find, then Delete Selected/Delete All); API: geom("geom1").defeaturing("ShortEdges").find() / delete(ftag) / deleteAll(ftag), or create("dse1", "DeleteShortEdges")

parameters.name: entsize
parameters.description: Maximum edge length (default 1e-3).

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Objects to search.

parameters.name: delete
parameters.description: all | selected (feature property).

tools.notes: Virtual operations (Ignore Edges, Collapse Edges) are an alternative when the CAD kernel cannot heal the model.

tools.name: Delete Sliver Faces (CAD defeaturing)
tools.description: Finds long, narrow faces narrower than a maximum width (typical of CAD translation artifacts and small offsets between surfaces) and removes them by growing the neighboring faces. Removing slivers avoids extremely thin, poor-quality mesh elements.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Delete Sliver Faces; API: geom("geom1").defeaturing("SliverFaces").find()/delete(ftag)/deleteAll(ftag) or create("dsl1", "DeleteSliverFaces")

parameters.name: entsize
parameters.description: Maximum face width (default 1e-3).

parameters.name: input / delete
parameters.description: Objects to search; delete all or selected.

tools.notes: Available with CAD Import Module, Design Module and CAD LiveLinks (CAD kernel only).

tools.name: Delete Small Faces (CAD defeaturing)
tools.description: Finds faces smaller than a maximum size and collapses them into adjacent faces, edges or vertices, removing tiny details such as small patches or imprints that would force local mesh refinement. Each deletion is recorded as a DeleteSmallFaces feature in the geometry sequence.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Delete Small Faces; API: geom("geom1").defeaturing("SmallFaces").find()/delete(ftag)/deleteAll(ftag) or create("dsf1", "DeleteSmallFaces")

parameters.name: entsize
parameters.description: Maximum face size (default 1e-3).

parameters.name: input / delete
parameters.description: Objects to search; delete all or selected.

tools.notes: Check the result with a mesh preview; collapsing faces can slightly change volumes and areas.

tools.name: Delete Spikes (CAD defeaturing)
tools.description: Finds and removes spikes - narrow protrusions of a face boundary narrower than a maximum width - by trimming the face, cleaning up translation artifacts that otherwise produce slender elements. It works like the other defeaturing finders: search by size, review, then delete selected or all.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Delete Spikes; API: geom("geom1").defeaturing("DeleteSpikes").find()/delete(ftag)/deleteAll(ftag) or create("dsp1", "DeleteSpikes")

parameters.name: entsize
parameters.description: Maximum spike width (default 1e-3).

parameters.name: input / delete
parameters.description: Objects to search; delete all or selected.

tools.notes: Demo file defeaturing_demo_7.x_b in the CAD Import Module Application Library illustrates spikes.

tools.name: Detach Faces (CAD defeaturing)
tools.description: Removes selected faces from a CAD object (parent) and forms a new object (child) from them, healing the parent wound by extending adjacent faces or capping, and the child by filling or patching. Typical uses are separating a feature (a boss, a hole volume) into its own domain for different materials or mesh control.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Detach Faces; API: geom("geom1").create("det1", "DetachFaces") or defeaturing("DetachFaces").delete(ftag)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Faces to detach.

parameters.name: healparent
parameters.description: fill | patch (default) - Create capping faces or Extend adjacent faces in the parent.

parameters.name: healchild
parameters.description: fill | patchchild | patchparent (default) - how the child object is closed.

tools.notes: Only for CAD (Parasolid) objects.

tools.name: Replace Faces (CAD defeaturing)
tools.description: Deletes selected faces and closes the resulting wound either by extending/shrinking the surrounding faces or by creating capping faces, which removes features such as bosses, pockets, embossed text or holes (optionally treated as through holes). It is the general-purpose manual defeaturing tool when the automatic finders do not recognize a detail.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Defeaturing and Repair > Replace Faces; API: geom("geom1").create("rfa1", "ReplaceFaces")

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Faces to replace.

parameters.name: heal
parameters.description: extend (default) | cap.

parameters.name: throughhole
parameters.description: Heal as if the removed faces were a through hole.

tools.notes: Delete Fillets and Delete Holes (existing entries) are specialized finders for those feature types.

tools.name: Defeaturing tools API: defeaturing(tool).find() / detail() / delete() / deleteAll()
tools.description: Programmatic interface behind the Defeaturing tools window: for tools Fillets, Holes, ShortEdges, SliverFaces, SmallFaces and Spikes (DeleteSpikes) you set the input objects and size limits, call find() to populate detail(), inspect groups (size, groupNames, groupEntities, groupObject), select subsets with setGroup/addGroup/removeGroup, and call delete(ftag) or deleteAll(ftag) to append the corresponding Delete... feature to the geometry sequence.
tools.usage: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").defeaturing("Fillets"|"Holes"|"ShortEdges"|"SliverFaces"|"SmallFaces"|"DeleteSpikes"|"DetachFaces"|"ReplaceFaces")

parameters.name: selection("input").set(onames)
parameters.description: Objects to examine.

parameters.name: set("entsize", s) / set("minentsize", s)
parameters.description: Maximum detail size (and minimum radius for Fillets/Holes).

parameters.name: find()
parameters.description: Search for details in the size interval.

parameters.name: detail().size() / groupNames() / groupEntities(n) / groupObject(n)
parameters.description: Inspect found details.

parameters.name: delete(ftag) / deleteAll(ftag)
parameters.description: Create and build a deletion feature for selected or all details.

tools.notes: Found details are ordered by size; each delete call inserts the feature after the current one and builds it.

tools.name: ECAD import: IPC-2581 and ODB++ printed circuit boards
tools.description: Geometry Import of PCB layouts from IPC-2581 (.xml) or ODB++ (archive or directory) files (ecadtype ipc2581 / odb++): copper and dielectric layers, vias/drills and the board outline are read and extruded into 3D using the layer stackup, with grouping All (single object), By layer, or No grouping. In 6.4 a Preview button shows copper and drill layers and nets for selecting what to import, and Pads settings create pad domains/faces for chosen components and pins.
tools.usage: Geometry > Import > Source: ECAD file > Browse > (Preview) > Import; API: geom("geom1").create("imp1", "Import"); set("filename", "board.xml"); importData()

parameters.name: grouping
parameters.description: all | layer (default) | none.

parameters.name: importtype
parameters.description: full3d (copper with thickness) | shell (metal as embedded boundaries).

parameters.name: importlayer / layername / height / elevation
parameters.description: Per-layer import flags, names, thicknesses and z-positions.

parameters.name: Nets to Import / Pads / Net selections per layer
parameters.description: 6.4 net filtering, pad creation and layer-net selections.

parameters.name: updategeomunit
parameters.description: Use the unit from the file (mil switches the sequence to inch).

tools.notes: Many PCB exports lack thickness data; check the Layers table before importing. Refresh Data from File reloads layers and nets after the file changes.

tools.name: ECAD import: GDS-II layouts (IC and MEMS)
tools.description: Imports GDS-II (.gds) mask layouts (ecadtype gds) in 2D or 3D, selecting the cell to import (top cell by default) and optionally filtering by subcell, grouping By layer or No grouping, and extruding layers as Full 3D or Metal shell. GDS files carry no thickness or unit information, so layer thicknesses and elevations must be entered (unit shown as um).
tools.usage: Geometry > Import > ECAD file (.gds) > Cell to import / Filter by subcell > Layers to import table (thickness, elevation) > Import

parameters.name: Cell to import / Filter by subcell
parameters.description: Hierarchy level to import and subcell type filter.

parameters.name: grouping
parameters.description: layer (default) | none ('all' not recommended for GDS).

parameters.name: height / elevation
parameters.description: Layer thicknesses (default 0) and z-positions.

parameters.name: repairtol
parameters.description: Relative repair tolerance (default 1e-5 for GDS).

tools.example: Import a GDS-II layout such as the sample bipolar_transistor.gds in the ECAD_Import_Module application folder: enter a thickness and elevation for each layer to import (GDS carries none), choose Type of import = Full 3D, Import, then Form Union and mesh layer by layer with swept meshes.
tools.notes: Use the 2D import for cross-section or layout-only studies to keep models small.

tools.name: ECAD layer stackup, elevations and short-edge cleanup options
tools.description: Import options that control how 2D layouts become a 3D board or chip: the Layers table (import flag, name, type, thickness, elevation), automatic or manual elevations (for example metal layer between dielectric layers), unite metal and in-layer dielectric, drill-layer handling, ignore vertices with continuous tangent and eliminate short edges (with angle tolerance and maximum edge length) to simplify meshing, keep interior boundaries, and creation of layer selections shown in physics. Correct stackup data is essential because many PCB and all GDS files lack layer thicknesses.
tools.usage: Import node (ECAD) > Layers / Layer Stackup / Advanced sections; API: set("height", ...), set("elevation", ...), set("ignorecontvtx", "on"), set("elimshortedg", "on"), set("maxedglen", ...), set("sellayer", "on")

parameters.name: ignorecontvtx / contangletol
parameters.description: Remove vertices on smooth outlines (tolerance 5 deg).

parameters.name: elimshortedg / maxedglen
parameters.description: Eliminate edges shorter than the given length.

parameters.name: intbnd
parameters.description: Keep interior boundaries within layers.

parameters.name: sellayer / sellayershow / createselection
parameters.description: Layer selections and where they are shown.

tools.notes: Geometries imported with these simplifications cannot be exported to 3D CAD formats with the removed vertices. Mesh PCBs layer by layer: swept meshes for metal, tetrahedra for dielectrics with vias.

tools.name: Export OASIS (ECAD Import Module)
tools.description: Exports 2D geometry objects (or work-plane objects from 3D, with a work plane to layer-number/name table) to the OASIS (.oas) layout format for mask and IC design tools, approximating curves with the graphics, coarse, normal or fine rendering detail. It requires an ECAD Import Module license.
tools.usage: Geometry > Export > File type: OASIS (*.oas); API: geom("geom1").export().setType("oasis"); export().setOasisApproxDetail("fine"); geom("geom1").export(filename) or exportFinal(filename)

parameters.name: setOasisApproxDetail
parameters.description: graphics (default) | coarse | normal | fine.

parameters.name: setLayerNumber / setLayerName
parameters.description: Layer assignment of each work plane when exporting from 3D.

tools.notes: Export entire finalized geometry is unavailable from 3D components; select work-plane objects instead.

tools.name: PCB to Material Data (add-in)
tools.description: ECAD Import Module add-in that replaces the detailed traces and vias of a PCB with a space-dependent interpolation function of homogenized material properties (heat capacity, density, thermal conductivity, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, thermal expansion) and builds a simplified geometry by extruding the board outline per the layer stack. It speeds up thermal and thermal-stress analyses of boards while optionally keeping selected components as domains.
tools.usage: Developer > Add-in Libraries > ECAD_Import_Module > pcb_to_material_data; then Developer > Add-ins > PCB to Material Data; select PCB file, review layers, assign trace/dielectric/via-core materials, create

parameters.name: Layers table
parameters.description: Names, types and thicknesses; unselected copper layers are approximated as dielectric.

parameters.name: Materials / Vias
parameters.description: Global or built-in materials with the six required constant properties.

parameters.name: Components
parameters.description: Optionally keep selected components as explicit domains.

tools.example: Select an IPC-2581 board file (for example the audioStreamingPCB.xml sample used by the ECAD Import Module tutorials), assign copper and FR4-type materials in the add-in, create the simplified board, then add Heat Transfer in Solids with component heat sources to get the board temperature map.
tools.notes: Only constant material values are supported for the homogenization.

tools.name: LiveLinkSOLIDWORKS geometry feature (synchronization, configurations, CAD parameters)
tools.description: Geometry sequence node that synchronizes the active or a specified SOLIDWORKS document into COMSOL: parameters named in param with values in paramexpr are sent to SOLIDWORKS, the model is rebuilt there (in the stored configuration and display state) and the resulting bodies are transferred associatively as CAD-kernel objects, optionally with material data and user-defined selections. Synchronization runs automatically during parametric sweeps and optimization studies.
tools.usage: Home > LiveLink > LiveLink for SOLIDWORKS > Synchronize; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("cad1", "LiveLinkSOLIDWORKS"); feature("cad1").importData(); feature("cad1").updateCadParamTable(add, repl)

parameters.name: synchronizewith / document / configuration / displaystate
parameters.description: active | specified document and its configuration/display state.

parameters.name: param / paramexpr / sync
parameters.description: Linked CAD dimensions or global variables, their COMSOL expressions and per-parameter sync flag.

parameters.name: keepsolid / keepbnd / keepfree
parameters.description: Object types to synchronize.

parameters.name: assocfaces / assocedges / assocvertices
parameters.description: Associativity per entity type (turn off edges/vertices for speed).

parameters.name: offline / selectsweep / requestfilename
parameters.description: Offline synchronization and sweep requests.

tools.notes: The CAD document must stay open in SOLIDWORKS during sweeps and optimizations. Only dimensions not defined by equations can be driven from COMSOL.

tools.name: LiveLinkAutoCAD geometry feature (LiveLink for AutoCAD)
tools.description: Synchronizes 3D solids, surfaces and curves from the active or specified AutoCAD drawing into the COMSOL geometry sequence, sending parameter values (dimensional constraints/parameters) to AutoCAD, regenerating and transferring the result associatively. The layer state of the drawing is recorded and reapplied on later synchronizations; only objects visible in AutoCAD are transferred.
tools.usage: Home > LiveLink > LiveLink for AutoCAD > Synchronize; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("cad1", "LiveLinkAutoCAD"); importData()

parameters.name: Synchronize with / Document
parameters.description: Active document or Specified document (keeps the last layer state).

parameters.name: Parameters in CAD package table
parameters.description: AutoCAD parameters linked through the COMSOL Parameter Selection window and their COMSOL values.

parameters.name: Objects to synchronize
parameters.description: Solids, surfaces, curves and points.

tools.example: Application Library LiveLink_for_AutoCAD/tuning_fork_llac (Geometric Parameter Optimization of a Tuning Fork): open tuning_fork.dwg in AutoCAD, synchronize with the LiveLink for AutoCAD node, and optimize the prong length so the fundamental eigenfrequency is 440 Hz.
tools.notes: Switch AutoCAD to the desired layer state, then choose Active document to synchronize a different state.

tools.name: LiveLinkRevit geometry feature and Synchronization Settings (LiveLink for Revit)
tools.description: Synchronizes building geometry from Revit into COMSOL: room volumes (extended to walls or to wall centerlines), room-bounding elements, elements inside rooms, conceptual masses rebuilt from COMSOL parameter values, or all elements visible in a 3D view. What is transferred is defined in Revit through named configurations in the Synchronization Settings window, created from scratch or from a view.
tools.usage: Revit: COMSOL Multiphysics tab > Synchronization Settings (configurations, New from View, Preview); COMSOL: Home > LiveLink > LiveLink for Revit > Synchronize; API: geom("geom1").create("cad1", "LiveLinkRevit")

parameters.name: Configuration (active)
parameters.description: Rooms or 3D view to synchronize; Save settings in project.

parameters.name: Synchronize view / Create selection
parameters.description: Transfer elements of a 3D view (walls layers, framing, equipment) with selections.

parameters.name: Room extension
parameters.description: Extend to walls (solid room volume) or Extend to wall centerline (surfaces).

parameters.name: Synchronize room bounding elements
parameters.description: Solids for walls, floors, ceilings, roofs.

tools.example: Application Library LiveLink_for_Revit/living_room_acoustics_llrevit: synchronize the living room from house_living_room.rvt and compute its room acoustics with pressure acoustics on the synchronized geometry.
tools.notes: Room synchronization can fail if walls, floors and ceilings are not Room Bounding; add Room Separators where needed. Use two LiveLink nodes to combine room volumes and 3D-view elements.

tools.name: LiveLinkInventor geometry feature and COMSOL Component Selection window (LiveLink for Inventor)
tools.description: Synchronizes Inventor parts and assemblies into COMSOL with parameter control; for assemblies the COMSOL Component Selection window in Inventor decides whether all Visible components or a Selected set from the assembly tree (including hidden ones, never suppressed ones) are transferred. The choice is saved in the Inventor file.
tools.usage: Inventor: COMSOL Multiphysics tab > Parameters / Selections / Components; COMSOL: Home > LiveLink > LiveLink for Inventor; API: geom("geom1").create("cad1", "LiveLinkInventor")

parameters.name: Synchronize (Component Selection)
parameters.description: Visible (default) or Selected components.

parameters.name: param / paramexpr
parameters.description: Linked Inventor parameters and their values.

tools.example: Application Library LiveLink_for_Inventor/bracket_optimization_llinventor: optimize bracket dimensions with the Parameter Optimization study while Inventor regenerates bracket_optimization.ipt at each iteration.
tools.notes: The same Components window concept exists for Solid Edge and PTC Creo Parametric assemblies.

tools.name: LiveLinkSolidEdge geometry feature (LiveLink for Solid Edge)
tools.description: Bidirectional associative link to Solid Edge parts and assemblies: COMSOL sends variable values, Solid Edge rebuilds, and the geometry returns as CAD-kernel objects with selections, materials and associativity preserved, including automatic resynchronization during sweeps and optimizations. Parameters, selections and assembly components are prepared on the COMSOL Multiphysics tab inside Solid Edge.
tools.usage: Solid Edge: COMSOL Multiphysics tab (Parameter Selection, Selections, Components, Synchronize Offline); COMSOL: Home > LiveLink > LiveLink for Solid Edge; API: geom("geom1").create("cad1", "LiveLinkSolidEdge")

parameters.name: Synchronize with / Document
parameters.description: Active or specified Solid Edge document.

parameters.name: param / paramexpr / sync
parameters.description: Linked variables and values.

tools.example: Application Library LiveLink_for_Solid_Edge/pipe_fitting_llse (Stress Analysis of a Pipe Fitting from a CAD File): the threaded fitting assembly is synchronized from Solid Edge and a 2D axisymmetric cross section is derived for the stress analysis.
tools.notes: Solid Edge must be running with the document open while COMSOL solves.

tools.name: LiveLinkPTCCreoParametric geometry feature (LiveLink for PTC Creo Parametric)
tools.description: Associative synchronization with PTC Creo Parametric parts and assemblies, driving Creo parameters and dimensions from COMSOL parameters, rebuilding in Creo and transferring the geometry with selections and materials. Supports Component Selection for assemblies and offline synchronization files.
tools.usage: Creo: COMSOL Multiphysics tab; COMSOL: Home > LiveLink > LiveLink for PTC Creo Parametric; API: geom("geom1").create("cad1", "LiveLinkPTCCreoParametric")

parameters.name: param / paramexpr / sync
parameters.description: Linked Creo parameters and COMSOL expressions.

parameters.name: Synchronize with / Document
parameters.description: Active or specified model.

tools.example: Application Library LiveLink_for_PTC_Creo_Parametric/induction_motor_llcreop (Two-Pole Three-Phase Induction Motor): the skewed squirrel-cage motor assembly is synchronized from Creo and the magnetic field is computed on several cross sections along the axis.
tools.notes: Creo 12 files can also be imported without the LiveLink on supported Windows/Linux platforms via the CAD Import Module.

tools.name: COMSOL Parameter Selection window (CAD LiveLink add-in)
tools.description: Window on the COMSOL Multiphysics tab inside the CAD program (SOLIDWORKS, AutoCAD, Inventor, Solid Edge, Creo, Revit) where CAD dimensions and global variables are picked from the feature tree and added to the 'Parameters to add to COMSOL model' list; after saving the CAD file they appear in the LiveLink node's parameter table. Only parameters not driven by equations can be controlled from COMSOL, but equation-driven ones can still be read.
tools.usage: CAD program > COMSOL Multiphysics tab > Parameter Selection > select feature > choose dimensions > Add > OK > save CAD file

parameters.name: Available Dimensions and Equations
parameters.description: Dimensions/variables of the selected feature or Equations folder.

parameters.name: Parameters to add to COMSOL model
parameters.description: Linked list saved in the CAD file (Revert to Saved, Delete, Clear).

tools.example: In SOLIDWORKS select Sketch1 of the bracket, add D1@Sketch1 and D2@Boss-Extrude1, save the part; in COMSOL click Synchronize and map them to the global parameters w and t.
tools.notes: Installing the COMSOL Client also registers the CAD add-in for preparing designs and running apps.

tools.name: COMSOL Selections window (CAD LiveLink add-in)
tools.description: CAD-side window for defining named selections of bodies, components, features, faces, edges or points that are transferred with the geometry as COMSOL selections, so physics and materials can be assigned to stable named sets that survive design changes. Material-based selections can also be generated automatically.
tools.usage: CAD program > COMSOL Multiphysics tab > Selections (or right-click an entity > COMSOL Selections) > New > add entities > OK before synchronizing

parameters.name: Selections / Entities
parameters.description: Named selections, each of one entity type.

parameters.name: Generate selections from materials
parameters.description: Create selections per CAD material (on by default).

tools.example: Create a 'coolant_faces' selection on the inner faces of a cold plate in SOLIDWORKS; after synchronization use it directly as the boundary selection of a Heat Flux node.
tools.notes: Selections are stored in the CAD file on the next save.

tools.name: Offline synchronization (COMSOL Synchronize Offline window, CAD LiveLinks)
tools.description: Workflow for when COMSOL and the CAD program cannot run together: from the CAD side, save an Initial synchronization file with the current geometry (optionally materials, chosen object types and associativity), or load a request file written by the COMSOL LiveLink node (for specific parameter values or a whole parametric sweep) and save a Requested synchronization file containing all generated geometries. The LiveLink node then loads the file offline.
tools.usage: CAD program > Tools > COMSOL > Offline Synchronization (Synchronization: Initial | Requested); COMSOL LiveLink node: offline = on, request file for a sweep (selectsweep = std1/param)

parameters.name: Synchronization
parameters.description: Initial (current geometry) or Requested (from a request file).

parameters.name: Synchronize material data / Solids / Surfaces / Curves and points
parameters.description: Content of the file.

parameters.name: Associativity for vertices and edges
parameters.description: Turn off to speed up large geometries.

tools.example: On a cluster without SOLIDWORKS: in COMSOL write a request for the sweep std1/param, open it on a CAD workstation in the Synchronize Offline window, save the requested synchronization file, and load it in the LiveLink node before submitting the batch job.
tools.notes: receivefilename, sweepfilename and receivecount properties report the loaded offline data.

tools.name: Running COMSOL applications from CAD software (LiveLink + COMSOL Server)
tools.description: CAD LiveLinks let users launch COMSOL apps (Application Builder MPH apps that use the LiveLink node) from the Run Application button on the CAD program's COMSOL Multiphysics tab, or, with a COMSOL Server license and the COMSOL Client, connect to a COMSOL Server and run apps that synchronize the open CAD design. Designers can thus evaluate simulations without the Model Builder.
tools.usage: CAD program > COMSOL Multiphysics tab > Run Application (COMSOL Multiphysics installation) or COMSOL Client > log in to COMSOL Server > launch app

parameters.name: COMSOL Client
parameters.description: Downloadable client that installs the CAD add-in and connects to COMSOL Server.

parameters.name: Run Application
parameters.description: Disabled when only the COMSOL Client is installed.

tools.example: Application Library LiveLink_for_SOLIDWORKS/Applications/bike_frame_analyzer_llsw: a runnable app shipped with the frame part mountainbike_hardtail.SLDPRT; open the part in SOLIDWORKS, then start the app with Run Application on the COMSOL Multiphysics tab.
tools.notes: The CAD document must be open before starting an app that synchronizes geometry.

tools.name: COMSOL tab in Excel: linked Definitions (parameters, variables, functions)
tools.description: LiveLink for Excel adds a COMSOL ribbon tab whose Definitions group inserts model parameters (all or per Parameters node), variables and functions into the worksheet as cell ranges linked to the model by a cell comment. Edited values update the model (automatically for parameters, or with Update / Update All / Select), so a workbook can act as the input sheet of a COMSOL model that is solved on a COMSOL Multiphysics server.
tools.usage: Excel > COMSOL tab > Open Linked / (Backstage) Open model > Definitions > Parameters | Variables | Functions > edit cells > Update; Study > Compute or select a study

parameters.name: Parameters / Parameters Nodes
parameters.description: Insert all global parameters or those of one node.

parameters.name: Update / Update All / Select
parameters.description: Push worksheet values into the model.

parameters.name: Break Link / Break All Links
parameters.description: Remove the linking comments.

parameters.name: COMSOL Desktop button
parameters.description: Open the same server model in the COMSOL Desktop.

tools.example: Application Library LiveLink_for_Excel/busbar_llexcel: open busbar_llexcel.xlsx, Open Linked loads busbar_llexcel.mph, change the busbar width cell, Compute, and the linked maximum-temperature cell updates.
tools.notes: A workbook links to one model at a time; the model path is stored in a cell comment.

tools.name: Numerical results in Excel (Derived Values, Point Evaluation, Results Parameters, plots)
tools.description: Numerical Results group of the Excel COMSOL tab that inserts results into the worksheet: Results > Parameters (evaluate without re-solving), Derived Values nodes, Point Evaluation at worksheet-defined coordinates, and 1D plot data or images via the Graphics group; all ranges stay linked and refresh with Update after recomputing. This turns a worksheet into a live results report for the linked model.
tools.usage: Excel > COMSOL tab > Numerical Results > Parameters | Derived Values | Point Evaluation (choose dataset, points, expression) > Update

parameters.name: Derived Values
parameters.description: Evaluate a model Derived Values node into the active cell.

parameters.name: Point Evaluation
parameters.description: Dataset, point coordinates and expression.

parameters.name: Update
parameters.description: Refresh linked results after solving.

tools.example: Select cell D2, Point Evaluation on Study 1/Solution 1 with coordinates from A3:C20 and expression ec.Qh to tabulate Joule heating along a line (busbar_llexcel tutorial).
tools.notes: Corresponding VBA commands exist (e.g. ResultsDerivedValue, ResultsParameters) for automation.

tools.name: Sweep window (parametric sweeps from an Excel worksheet)
tools.description: Excel COMSOL-tab window that lists the parametric and auxiliary sweep parameters of a selected study, copies them to the worksheet as a linked range, and writes edited worksheet values back to the study with Update Model, so design tables maintained in Excel drive COMSOL sweeps. Auxiliary sweep values of study steps are listed as well.
tools.usage: Excel > COMSOL tab > Study > Sweep > choose Study > Copy to Worksheet / Update Model

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Study whose sweeps are shown.

parameters.name: Parameter value list / Range
parameters.description: Values and the linked worksheet range.

tools.example: Copy the sweep of Study 1 to the sheet, replace the width list by 5 new values in adjacent cells, select the linked cell, Sweep > Update Model, then Compute.
tools.notes: Lists containing range() or units are written to a single cell instead of one value per cell.

tools.name: Material Export from Excel to a COMSOL material library
tools.description: Converts worksheet material data (constant values or field-dependent tables such as temperature-dependent properties) into a COMSOL material library file: the Material Export Settings window maps worksheet property names to recognized COMSOL properties and units, and the library can be saved interactively or exported in batch. The resulting library appears in the COMSOL Material Browser like any other material library.
tools.usage: Excel > COMSOL tab > Material Export > Settings (Material names range, Property names range, Assign valid properties, units; Field dependent data tab) > Save Material Library

parameters.name: Material names range / Property names range
parameters.description: Column of material names and row of property names.

parameters.name: Valid properties (SI Units) / Unit
parameters.description: Mapping to COMSOL properties such as k, rho, Cp, sigma.

parameters.name: Sheet contains field dependent data
parameters.description: Field variable settings for tabulated dependencies.

tools.example: Sheet with alloys in column A and 'Thermal conductivity', 'Density', 'Heat capacity' in row 1: assign k, rho, Cp in Material Export Settings, save as alloys.mph library and load it from the COMSOL Material Browser.
tools.notes: Removing the linking comment on a material cell drops it from the export.

tools.name: Load from / Save to Excel workbook in COMSOL tables (loadFile / saveFile)
tools.description: With LiveLink for Excel, table-based settings in the COMSOL Desktop (parameters, variables, interpolation and piecewise functions, parametric/auxiliary sweeps, results tables, global control variables) gain Load from File / Save to File for .xlsx with sheet and cell-range options, working even when Excel is not installed. The same exchange is available through the API with loadFile/saveFile on the feature.
tools.usage: Table toolbar > Load from File / Save to File > Microsoft Excel Workbook (*.xlsx) > Sheet, Range, Overwrite, Include headers; API: model.param().loadFile("data.xlsx", "Sheet1", "A1"); feature.saveFile(filename, sheet, range, header, overwrite)

parameters.name: Sheet / Range
parameters.description: Worksheet name (default first) and top-left cell or range (empty = whole sheet).

parameters.name: Overwrite / Include headers
parameters.description: Replace or append; write table headers.

parameters.name: Separate units column / Calculated values
parameters.description: Extra columns for parameter import/export.

tools.notes: Formats: parameters = name, expression, [unit], [value], description; interpolation = argument, value; piecewise = start, end, expression; sweeps = name, space-separated list.

tools.name: COMSOL API for VBA (ComsolUtil, RibbonUtil, ModelUtil)
tools.description: COM interface of LiveLink for Excel for automating COMSOL from VBA macros: CreateObject("comsolcom.comsolutil") gives ComsolUtil (StartComsolServer, GetRibbonUtil), RibbonUtil exposes every ribbon action (OpenModel, Connect, IsConnected, Disconnect, Compute, Sweep, results insertion), and CreateObject("comsolcom.modelutil") gives ModelUtil for the full model API. A model can be saved as 'Model File for VBA' to obtain ready-made VBA commands.
tools.usage: Excel Developer tab > Visual Basic > Tools > References > ComsolCom 6.4; Set ComsolUtil = CreateObject("comsolcom.comsolutil"); Set RibbonUtil = ComsolUtil.GetRibbonUtil

parameters.name: ComsolUtil.StartComsolServer(useGraphics)
parameters.description: Start a local COMSOL Multiphysics server (default port 2036).

parameters.name: RibbonUtil.Connect([host], [port], [login], [pwd]) / IsConnected / Disconnect
parameters.description: Server connection management.

parameters.name: RibbonUtil.OpenModel
parameters.description: Common way to start/connect and load the linked model.

parameters.name: ModelUtil
parameters.description: Access to model.param, model.study(...).run and so on.

tools.example:
Sub RunBusbar()
  Dim ComsolUtil As ComsolUtil
  Dim RibbonUtil As IRibbonUtil
  Set ComsolUtil = CreateObject("comsolcom.comsolutil")
  Set RibbonUtil = ComsolUtil.GetRibbonUtil
  RibbonUtil.Connect
  Dim modelutil As Object
  Set modelutil = CreateObject("comsolcom.modelutil")
  ' model object from the server, then model.param.set / model.study("std1").run
End Sub
tools.notes: Save workbooks with macros as .xlsm. See the existing 'LiveLink for Excel' entry for the overall product.

tools.name: readExcelFile / writeExcelFile (Application Builder methods)
tools.description: Method-editor language elements added by LiveLink for Excel for applications: writeExcelFile writes a String[][] (numbers, text or Excel formulas in English format) to the first sheet or to a given sheet and start cell, and readExcelFile reads a sheet from a start cell into a String[][]. Files may be on the client or on the server via file schemes.
tools.usage: writeExcelFile(String filename, String[][] data); writeExcelFile(String filename, String sheet, String cell, String[][] data); String[][] readExcelFile(String filename); String[][] readExcelFile(String filename, String sheet, String cell)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Path or file scheme (e.g. user:///, temp:///).

parameters.name: sheet / cell
parameters.description: Target sheet and top-left cell.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: String matrix; formulas like "=SUM(A1:C1)" are allowed.

tools.notes: Tables in apps can also offer Load from file / Save to file with the Excel dialog.

tools.name: Cosimulation for Simulink (export node, SimulinkCosimulation)
tools.description: Global Definitions/Study node of LiveLink for Simulink that defines which global parameters are cosimulation inputs (changeable at every communication time), which are block parameters (set once at initialization), the output expressions and the time-dependent study to run, and exports this interface as an FMU-format cosimulation file used by the COMSOL Cosimulation block. The model itself stays in the MPH file.
tools.usage: Study tab or right-click Global Definitions > Cosimulation for Simulink > Inputs / Block Parameters / Outputs / Study > Export; API: model.externalInterface().create("sim1", "SimulinkCosimulation"); set("filename", ...); setIndex("inputname", ...); run()

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Cosimulation file to export (next to the MPH file by default).

parameters.name: inputname / inputvalue / inputunit
parameters.description: Input parameters and initial values, in block port order.

parameters.name: Block parameters
parameters.description: Parameters evaluated only at initialization (e.g. material constants).

parameters.name: Outputs / study
parameters.description: Global output expressions and the time-dependent study step.

tools.notes: Save the MPH file before exporting. Do not use geometry or mesh parameters as inputs. Simulink need not be installed on the exporting computer.

tools.name: COMSOL Cosimulation block (Simulink library)
tools.description: Simulink block from the 'COMSOL 6.4' library section that loads a cosimulation file exported from COMSOL and exposes its inputs and outputs as ports. At each communication step Simulink sends inputs, COMSOL advances its own time-dependent solver from t to t+dt with consistent initialization, and returns outputs, so control logic in Simulink can act on a full finite-element plant model.
tools.usage: Simulink Library Browser > COMSOL 6.4 > COMSOL Cosimulation; double-click > Filename (searched in MATLAB current folder, the diagram folder and mphsimsettings paths), Communication step size, Block Parameters

parameters.name: Filename
parameters.description: Exported cosimulation (FMU) file.

parameters.name: Communication step size
parameters.description: Interval at which Simulink and COMSOL exchange data.

parameters.name: Block Parameters
parameters.description: Override default block-parameter values (units informative only).

tools.example: Drag COMSOL Cosimulation into the diagram, set Filename thermal_actuator.fmu and communication step 0.1 s, connect a Relay (on/off controller) from the displacement output to the voltage input, and run the simulation.
tools.notes: Simulink controls the overall time stepping; COMSOL may take several internal steps per communication step. After the run the model can be saved and postprocessed in COMSOL.

tools.name: mphsimsettings / mphupdatesystem (LiveLink for Simulink)
tools.description: MATLAB functions shipped with LiveLink for Simulink: mphsimsettings opens a preferences UI to add model search paths, show the COMSOL progress bar and force reloading the model before each cosimulation, and mphupdatesystem updates all COMSOL Cosimulation blocks (and FMUs) in a Simulink system to the running LiveLink version, with backup options. Use them after installing a new COMSOL version or when cosimulation files are stored outside the MATLAB path.
tools.usage: mphsimsettings; mphupdatesystem(system); mphupdatesystem(system, 'librarypath', path, 'updateversion', '6.4', 'createbackup', 'on', 'postupdateaction', 'save')

parameters.name: createbackup / overwritebackup
parameters.description: Backup of modified files.

parameters.name: updateblock / updatefmu
parameters.description: Update blocks and/or FMUs (default on).

parameters.name: postupdateaction
parameters.description: open | save (default) the updated system.

parameters.name: librarypath / updateversion
parameters.description: Additional library path and target version.

tools.notes: Start MATLAB through 'COMSOL Multiphysics 6.4 with Simulink' (or comsol mphserver simulink on Linux) so these functions and the server are available.

tools.name: Starting COMSOL Multiphysics with Simulink
tools.description: LiveLink for Simulink requires MATLAB to be started together with a COMSOL Multiphysics server in a preconfigured way: on Windows via the 'COMSOL Multiphysics 6.4 with Simulink' shortcut, on macOS via the corresponding application, and on Linux with 'comsol mphserver simulink'. Manual connection setup is not supported.
tools.usage: Windows: Start menu > COMSOL Multiphysics 6.4 > COMSOL Multiphysics 6.4 with Simulink; Linux/macOS terminal: comsol mphserver simulink

parameters.name: Connected MATLAB installation
parameters.description: Can be changed after installation (see Changing the Connected MATLAB Installation).

parameters.name: Floating network license
parameters.description: Each server session checks out licenses; see the license note in the guide.

tools.example:
comsol mphserver simulink
% MATLAB opens with the COMSOL server in the background; click the Simulink button and open thermal_actuator_llsimulink.slx
tools.notes: The Simulink window is not opened automatically.
